findings.title: Shutdown timeout resumes finalization while admitted releases still need Python
findings.scenario: A foreign-thread producer deleter sleeps 5.5 seconds, releasing the GIL. The five-second exit wait returns with in_flight=1. Normal CPython 3.12 finalization starts; the finite deleter wakes and re-acquires the GIL. The process aborts (rc -6, FATAL: exception not rethrown).
findings.fix: Keep finalization behind quiescence for every admitted Python-dependent release. A timeout may log diagnostics but must not return to ordinary finalization with admitted releases running. If bounded process exit is required, define a separate explicit process-exit policy; leaking a manager cannot cancel a deleter already running. Add a normal-exit overrun regression without os._exit.

findings.title: Aggregate deferred-release byte totals use unchecked signed additions
findings.scenario: Two individually valid disjoint fp32 descriptors each have shape (2**61-1,), bytes 9223372036854775804. The per-call e.bytes sum overflows int64. Independently, actual note_push with 4 pending bytes plus one such entry overflows. These are synthetic metadata boundaries, not demonstrated resident GPU allocations; an overflowing negative total can bypass the byte-bound drain.
findings.fix: Check aggregate operand bytes before the first launch, where overflow can raise ValueError safely. Make queue accounting and the bound comparison overflow-safe without throwing from the release destructor (check remaining headroom or drain before addition). Do not add a throwing ck_add in the destructor.
